events.title: Thomas v. Humboldt County: Certiorari denied; Gorsuch statement on Seventh Amendment incorporation
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied certiorari in THOMAS, CORRINE MORGAN, ET AL. v. HUMBOLDT COUNTY, CALIFORNIA, ET AL. (Docket 24-1180), a case concerning the Seventh Amendment right to a civil jury trial. Justice Gorsuch issued a statement respecting the denial, agreeing that vehicle problems made the case unsuitable for review but arguing that the underlying precedent—Minneapolis & St. Louis R. Co. v. Bombolis (1916), which held that the Seventh Amendment is not enforceable against the States—warrants reconsideration. Gorsuch noted that Bombolis is "something of a relic" and that modern incorporation doctrine has extended most Bill of Rights protections to the States. He argued that the Seventh Amendment should be incorporated against the States via the Fourteenth Amendment, as it was deeply rooted in American constitutional tradition and is now recognized as fundamental to checking governmental overreach.
events.why_relevant: Gorsuch's statement signals potential openness to overruling a century-old precedent denying Seventh Amendment incorporation, which could expand civil jury trial rights against state and local agencies and affect the balance of power between citizens and government in administrative proceedings.

events.summary: The White House issued a fact sheet on October 17, 2025, announcing that President Trump signed a proclamation invoking Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 to impose tariffs on imports of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, parts, and buses. The proclamation imposes a 25% tariff on medium- and heavy-duty trucks and truck parts (with USMCA-compliant vehicles subject to tariffs only on non-U.S. content) and a 10% tariff on buses. The administration states the tariffs are justified on national security grounds and include offset programs for domestic manufacturers through 2030.
events.why_relevant: The proclamation asserts executive authority to impose significant trade tariffs on a major industrial sector using national security justification under Section 232, a mechanism that expands presidential power over trade policy and potentially affects supply chains, consumer costs, and international trade relationships.

events.title: Trump issued proclamation imposing 25% tariff on medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and parts, 10% on buses
events.summary: President Trump signed Proclamation 10926 on October 17, 2025, imposing a 25 percent ad valorem tariff on imports of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles (MHDVs) and specified MHDV parts, and a 10 percent tariff on buses, effective November 1, 2025. The proclamation invokes Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, citing national security grounds. It establishes an import adjustment offset program for U.S.-assembled vehicles, allows tariff reductions for USMCA-qualifying goods based on U.S. content, and directs the Secretary of Commerce to monitor imports and potentially add additional parts to the tariff scope.
events.why_relevant: The proclamation asserts executive authority to impose broad tariffs on a major industrial sector using national security rationale, expanding presidential power over trade and potentially affecting supply chains, manufacturing, and consumer costs while bypassing congressional trade authority.
events.basis: I concur with the Secretary's finding that imports of MHDVs, certain MHDVPs, and buses threaten to impair the national security of the United States" and "impose a tariff system...to adjust imports of MHDVs, certain MHDVPs, and buses so that such imports will not threaten to impair the national security.

events.title: Alaska Health Department's Project Hope Organizes Naloxone Kit Build Event
events.summary: The Alaska Health Department's Project Hope organized a naloxone kit build event at the Fairview Recreation Center in Anchorage. The event brought together health, community, and military organizations, including the Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium, the Alaska Military Youth Academy, and the National Guard. Participants assembled kits containing naloxone, rubber gloves, mouth covers for rescue breaths, and instructions. The initiative aims to address the rising overdose deaths in Alaska by expanding access to naloxone, a medication that can reverse opioid overdoses.
events.why_relevant: This event is significant as it represents a coordinated effort to combat the opioid crisis in Alaska, where overdose deaths are increasing, by enhancing community access to life-saving medication.

events.title: Chicago's Health Department Issues Alerts on Drug Adulterants

The alerts aim to inform both the public and healthcare providers about the risks associated with these substances, enabling better prevention and treatment of overdoses.
